Timed to the SeaWorld trip — the family is at SeaWorld today (Fri Nov 13), so the tower lands on the actual park day, the same trip-timing as Pirate (park day) and Brick (park day). v2.97 (2026-11-12, evening run): 96th tower 'Octopus' (round head over two wide body bands with four dangling arms, 30 blocks, 7 clusters sizes 8/7/7/2/2/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates) + 93rd co-play prompt (be an octopus together — wiggle your arms like wiggly octopus arms saying 'wiggle… wiggle!', spin around slowly, touch the ground, then rest like a sleepy octopus; take turns; an octopus has eight arms — count the first three together: one, two, three!; pretend only, no real water, real octopuses are look, don't touch; at SeaWorld, look for the octopus waving its arms together). Octopus-play research: at 2, 'wiggle 8 arms like an octopus' is the canonical sea-animal movement (feet planted, arms only, waving like tentacles); the octopus fingerplay/song is spin around, touch the ground, wiggle eight arms, squirt your ink — adapted here as wiggle + slow spin + touch ground + rest, with the ink-squirt dropped as too abstract and the counting kept to the 1–3 subitizing range. Shark-play research: at 2, the shark dance form is a big arm-jaw chomp plus a little finger chomp and a fin on the head (the 'become the shark' move); 'chomp' is the entry word, and 'swim fast or slow?' is the tempo contrast; the arm-jaw chomp is distinct from Crab's hand-claw snap and Star's finger open/shut. Timed to the SeaWorld trip — the family visits SeaWorld tomorrow (Fri Nov 13), so the tower lands the day before, the same trip-timing as Dolphin (SeaWorld-eve). v2.95 (2026-11-12, morning run): 94th tower 'Brick' (three studs over four solid bands, 34 blocks, 7 clusters sizes 7/7/7/7/2/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates) + 91st co-play prompt (build with real bricks together — stack big bricks saying 'up… up… up!', count the studs — one, two, three! — then knock it down saying 'crash… down!', then sit down and stack it back up slowly and rest; take turns adding a brick; big bricks only — little LEGO bricks are too small for little hands, grown-up builds with those; at LEGOLAND, look for the giant bricks together). Brick-play research: at 2, stacking and pulling apart big bricks builds fine motor and hand-eye coordination; building it up and smashing it down is the fun part (the knock-down is the payoff); counting studs and sorting by colour is early math; Duplo-sized bricks are made for small hands with no small parts. Dolphin-play research: the leap is the dolphin's signature movement toddlers copy (arms together, arch up, jump/splash down); clicks and whistles are the dolphin sounds, and the echolocation clap game (dolphin claps twice, fish answer) is a copyable clap-exchange at 2; dolphins swim together in pods and help each other — the social form is togetherness. Timed to the LEGOLAND trip — SeaWorld is Fri Nov 13, so the tower lands the day before the park visit, the same trip-timing as Airplane (flight day), Dragon (park-eve), and Pirate (park day). v2.93 (2026-11-11, evening run): 92nd tower 'Pirate' (green hat tip over a red brim, a face with a blue patch band, a green shirt, on two blue boots, 31 blocks, 7 clusters sizes 7/7/7/3/3/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates) + 89th co-play prompt (play pirates together — put on a paper pirate hat or a bandana saying 'arrr… arrr!', rock side to side like you're sailing saying 'sail… sail!', then follow the treasure map: hide a favourite toy under a pillow together and find it saying 'treasure… found it!'; take turns being the captain; no toy swords — a soft parrot on your shoulder works instead, and a grown-up hides the treasure). Pirate-play research: the first treasure hunt is the toddler pirate form (hide one favourite toy, help him find it) and the map is what makes it a pirate hunt rather than a hiding game, keeping it distinct from the Stocking tower's hide-and-find; 'arrr'/'ahoy' are the sound words at the moment of motion; the paper hat is the one-prop costume and toy swords stay out. Dragon-play research: wing-flapping is the dragon's signature move (paper dragons with brad wings, Lamaze Flip Flap dragon, fans/scarves waved like wings); the roar is the sound word at the moment of motion, modelled by the parent, friendly never scary; fire breath is pretend blowing at tissue (no real flames) and the cave is the settle. Timed to the LEGOLAND trip — the dragon is the park's signature ride/character, so the tower lands the day before the park visit. v2.91 (2026-11-11, morning run): 90th tower 'Airplane' (nose tip over a nose, a full-width wing band, a fuselage, and two tail fins, 21 blocks, 5 clusters sizes 7/6/4/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates) + 87th co-play prompt (play airplanes together — arms out wide like wings saying 'vroom… vroom!', run a little way saying 'up… up… up!', then slow down and land together saying 'down… down!', taking turns being the pilot; on a real plane ride, look out the window together and point at the clouds — arms-out flying works in your seat too). Airplane-play research: arms-out flying plus takeoff-and-landing is gross-motor work (balance, coordination, spatial awareness) that teaches up/down and fast/slow; 'vroom' and 'up, up, up!' are the entry words modelled at the moment of motion; pretend flying gives a sense of control and adventure, which can ease travel-day nerves. v2.90 (2026-11-10, evening run): 89th tower 'Elf' (floppy pointed hat over ears and a face, a body with a belt, on two boots, 24 blocks, 8 clusters sizes 6/4/3/3/2/2/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates) + 86th co-play prompt (play Santa's workshop together — put on a pointy elf hat, a paper cone works, then make a toy for your teddy by stacking real blocks, tap it together, wrap it in paper and put it in the bag; take turns being the elf who makes it and Santa who checks it; a paper cone or a soft hat is the whole costume, no little bells on shoes, grown-up holds any real tools). Elf-play research: Santa's workshop is the elf's form — elves make toys with building blocks and wrap them, and taking turns being the maker and the checker is the teamwork; the pointed hat is the one-prop costume, no bells for under-3s. Sleigh was considered and rejected this run: the Sled tower (2026-11-06) already covers pull-along play with a blanket, so a sleigh would duplicate it. v2.89 (2026-11-10, afternoon run): 88th tower 'Santa' (red hat over a face and red suit with a green gift bag at his side on two boots, 28 blocks, 6 clusters sizes 6/6/10/2/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates) + 85th co-play prompt (play Santa together — put on a red hat saying 'ho… ho… ho!', carry a little bag and give a soft toy to your teddy saying 'for you!', then take turns being Santa and saying 'thank you!'; a soft red hat or a scarf works as the costume, no real beard needed, grown-up holds the bag). Santa-play research: dress-up role-play (hat, red scarf, mini gift bag) is the Santa form toddlers copy; pretend play emerges at 2–3 and builds language, cooperation, and empathy — giving a toy to a teddy is early giving practice; 'ho ho ho' is the copyable sound word. v2.88 (2026-11-10, morning run): 87th tower 'Reindeer' (antler tips over a face and body on two feet, 28 blocks, 7 clusters sizes 4/4/6/4/6/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates) + 84th co-play prompt (play reindeer together — hands on head like antlers saying 'antlers in… antlers out!', prance around saying 'jingle, jingle!' and shake hands in the air like jingle bells, then stop and touch your nose like Rudolph's shiny red nose; real jingle bells stay with a grown-up — they're too small for little hands — so the jingling is pretend hands in the air, a big soft shaker works too). Reindeer-play research: antlers in/out (Reindeer Pokey) is a copyable bilateral hands-on-head move; prancing with hoof-click sounds and jingle-bell shaking puts the sound word at the moment of motion; small jingle bells are a choking hazard for under-3s, so the jingle stays pretend. v2.87 (2026-11-09, evening run): 86th tower 'Present' (bow loops and knot over a lid, a body with a centre ribbon stripe, and a base band, 32 blocks, 5 clusters sizes 8/8/6/6/4, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 83rd co-play prompt (wrap a soft toy in paper together saying 'wrap… wrap!', let Liam tear it open saying 'rip… rip… what's inside?', take turns wrapping and unwrapping; plain paper or a tea towel, no tape on little fingers, grown-up handles any scissors). Present-play research: tearing wrapping paper is multisensory cause-and-effect (crinkle, resistance, rip) that toddlers often love more than the gift itself; it builds fine motor (pincer grasp, bilateral hold-and-pull) and object permanence ('what's inside?' guessing); wrapping together is a giving moment, kept simple and safe. v2.86 (2026-11-09, afternoon run): 85th tower 'Stocking' (cuff over a narrow leg on a foot that juts to one side, 18 blocks, 4 clusters sizes 8/4/2/4, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 82nd co-play prompt (hang a stocking — or a big sock! — on a hook, hide a big soft toy inside saying 'where did it go?', reach in and pull it out saying 'peek-a-boo… there it is!', taking turns hiding and finding; only big soft toys go in, no coins, no small balls, no hard candy, grown-up does the hanging and checks what's inside). Stocking-play research: 'what's in the stocking?' is a guessing game (touch/smell/sound, then reveal, then reverse roles) that builds vocabulary, inference, and senses; hiding and finding is object permanence in action — start partially hidden, ask 'where did it go?', answer with positive surprise; stocking stuffers for under-3s must be too big to swallow (AAP/CPSC small-parts test). v2.85 (2026-11-09, morning run): 84th tower 'Christmas Tree' (star tip over tiered bands on a trunk, 16 blocks, 5 clusters sizes 4/4/2/2/4, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 81st co-play prompt (decorate a real tree together — hang big soft ornaments on the low branches, count them — one, two, three! — then put the star on top together and step back to look; soft felt/wood/plastic ornaments only, low branches, no glass or sharp hooks, grown-up handles lights and cords). Christmas-tree-decorating research: at 2 the honest form is soft, lightweight, unbreakable ornaments on low branches only; hanging doubles as counting/sorting by colour (1–3); one well-placed ornament beats ten rushed ones, and stepping back to look is the payoff. v2.84 (2026-11-08, evening run): 83rd tower 'Gingerbread' (round head over arms-out body on two legs, 24 blocks, 6 clusters sizes 8/8/2/2/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 80th co-play prompt (make a paper gingerbread friend, smell the cinnamon, stick on big buttons for eyes and tummy and count them — one, two, three! — then run, run like the gingerbread man and stop; grown-ups handle the glue and any real baking). Gingerbread-play research: cinnamon/ginger smell is the sensory hook, decorating a paper friend with large buttons is the fine-motor work, counting buttons while decorating is one-to-one correspondence at 1–3, and 'run, run!' is a slow indoor chase with a clear stop. Note: this run first drafted a Turkey tower + prompt, then caught that Turkey was already the 60th tower (2026-11-01) with its own prompt — both were reverted before shipping, and the batch pivoted to Gingerbread. v2.83 (2026-11-08, afternoon run): 82nd tower 'Coat' (hood over shoulders and body with sleeve edges over a hem row, 30 blocks, 4 clusters sizes 10/8/6/6, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 79th co-play prompt (Montessori coat flip on the floor, zipper up, hood by his feet, arms in, flip over his head; grown-up starts the zip, he pulls it up; hang it on its hook; coat goes on first — coat, boots, hat, then mittens). Coat-play research: at 2, a child can take off an unfastened coat, find armholes, and put on a front-opening coat (no fastening); the coat flip is the canonical self-dressing move; undressing is easier than dressing, so taking it off and hanging it up is the part he can do himself. v2.82 (2026-11-08, morning run): 81st tower 'Boots' (two pull-handles over two shafts on a wide feet band over a two-colour sole row, 22 blocks, 4 clusters sizes 8/8/3/3, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 78th co-play prompt (pull rain boots on by their handles, stomp in a puddle, take them off and line them up by the door; boots go on second — coat, boots, hat, then mittens). Boots-play research: oversized pull handles plus a wide opening make pulling boots on a solo job for a toddler; stomping in puddles is the payoff; light and flexible beats heavy and stiff. v2.81 (2026-11-07, late run): 80th tower 'Hat' (pom + dome + brim band + two hanging earflaps, 22 blocks, 5 clusters sizes 6/6/6/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 77th co-play prompt (put a warm hat on/off, check it covers the ears, shake-head/look-up fit test, put it on a teddy too; dressing order coat, boots, hat, then mittens). Hat-play research: at 2, putting on a hat is one of the first dressing skills a child can actually do; the hat that stays on covers the ears and sits above the eyebrows; dressing is taught in small steps through dress-up play with no time pressure. v2.80 (2026-11-07, afternoon run): 79th tower 'Scarf' (rounded top over wide bands on two fringed ends, 22 blocks, 5 clusters sizes 6/6/6/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons) + 76th co-play prompt (drape a scarf like a cape, wrap a teddy snug, hide-and-find peek-a-boo; never tight around a little neck). Scarf-play research: cover/uncover builds object permanence, pulling off builds fine-motor grip, and a scarf is an open-ended prop (cape, doll blanket, den roof). One deep mechanic: tap a color cannon, blast matching block clusters, clear the tower. v2.79 (2026-11-07, parent report + browser test): fixed the leftover colored dot after a pop. The block and its white glyph were being removed correctly — the dot was a stuck pop particle. burst() used `var p` in a loop, so all six onfinish handlers closed over the same variable and only the last particle was ever removed; the other five sat at full opacity in the middle of the popped block (browser test: 4 blue dots, one per popped block, still there at 6s). Fixed with the same per-particle IIFE capture the ball code already uses, plus fill:'forwards' and a 900ms sweep so no particle can outlive the pop. Verified with a node closure test (old code removes 1 of 6, new code removes 6 of 6). v2.78 grew the cutscene rotation to 3 movies and retired frog-garden.
